title: U.S. Life Expectancy is Circling the Drain - Nautilus
gist: A Virginia Commonwealth University analysis by Steven H. Woolf of CDC and OECD data from 1999 to 2023 finds the US life expectancy gap with other developed countries is widening. The US fell from 14th place in 1980 (13 countries ahead) to 38th in 2023. The article says the US lacks the political will to address it.

insights.claim: In 1980 only 13 countries with populations over a million had higher life expectancy than the United States. By 2023 the US ranked 38th.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Falling relative longevity points to structural health-system underperformance, which affects insurers, pension and annuity assumptions, and labor supply.
insights.quote: According to data from 2023, we’re now 38th on that list.

insights.claim: The gap in life expectancy between the US and other developed countries has been widening for decades and is getting worse.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Mortality trends that keep diverging challenge longevity-risk models and life insurance pricing.
insights.quote: The chasm between life expectancy in the United States and other developed countries has been widening for some time, and it appears to be getting worse

insights.claim: Steven H. Woolf of Virginia Commonwealth University analyzed US life expectancy and age-based mortality from 1999 to 2023, using CDC, OECD and other data.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: A long-run, multi-source dataset makes the finding more credible for actuarial and policy use.
